kicker: Consumer · premium vs whole-company volume, Q2 FY27
title: Q2 volume grew at the top of the shelf
dek: Premium tiers outgrew the whole business in Q2 FY27: Radico's P&A volume +36% vs +7% overall, United Breweries +38% vs +16%, Campus 50%-plus vs +10%. ABD, which held prices on its mass brands, was the exception.

read: Price rises are pushing buyers off the bottom rung, not out of the market: where the cheap tier held its price, as at ABD, its volume came back.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls of the six companies named
notes: Volume growth is year-on-year for Q2 FY27 as disclosed on each company's call: Radico P&A 5.28 mn cases (+36%) vs IMFL volume above 10 mn cases (+7%); United Breweries premium beer (+38%) vs total volume (+16%); Campus shoes priced over ₹2,000 (above 50%, share of volume up from about 9% to 13%) vs 6.3 mn pairs in all (+10.2%); ABD Prestige & Above 4.5 mn cases (+6.1%) vs 10.0 mn cases (+11.1%), while its Mass Premium tier grew 15.5% with realisation up only 0.4%. United Breweries' Q2 was helped by a beer-tax cut in Karnataka, and Radico's Regular decline partly reflects state route-to-market and policy changes. United Spirits does not disclose segment volumes, and Relaxo did not give a volume figure; its 23% ASP rise against 11.6% revenue growth implies volume fell, which is a Vantage estimate.
